name: Yale Linus Smart Lock L2 (EU)

radios.note: Brochure lists Bluetooth 5.3 and Wi-Fi 2.4-5 GHz.

matter.note: Matter arrived by firmware update (lock firmware 2.0.20+, Yale Home app 2024.11.0+). Yale says Matter uses the lock's built-in Wi-Fi.

apple_home.note: Listed by Yale. Yale's troubleshooting pages mention occasional 'No response' issues in Apple Home.

home_assistant.note: Yale's Matter page does not list Home Assistant as a platform but names it as a Matter hub that exposes extra data such as DoorSense status.

hubRequired.note: Built-in Wi-Fi; Yale says only the partner platform's own hub or bridge is needed for Matter. The seller of this region's L2 should be checked: one non-official source mentions a separate Wi-Fi bridge for older EU units.

localControl.note: No Yale source states local-only control.

lockFit.note: Linus L2 attaches to the inside of the door over the existing cylinder, keeping your keys.

keypad.note: No keypad on the lock; the Yale Dot is a separate accessory.

power.note: Product title says rechargeable battery. One review mentions two 18650 cells charged via USB-C.

summary: The Yale Linus Smart Lock L2 is a retrofit lock for European doors with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. A firmware update added Matter over Wi-Fi, and Yale lists Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings as supported platforms. It runs on a rechargeable battery and has no keypad of its own; the Yale Dot is an optional accessory.
caveats: Matter needs lock firmware 2.0.20 or later and Yale Home app 2024.11.0 or later.
Yale says controlling the lock through a Matter hub is more limited than in the Yale Home app.
Yale's troubleshooting pages note Apple Home can report 'No response' after iOS updates.

sources.title: Yale Linus L2 Smart Lock with Built in Wi-Fi, Yale Dot and Rechargeable Battery Silver
